messages.text: I live in SW Oklahoma. It is already 95° 3/21/26. I would be planting the bombs in a very large pot, which shrubs are planted in other pots the same size. They come indoors in the winter. Would this be acceptable and would you give advice. I have been trying to start Milkweed from seed for a couple of years without success.

Hi Holly,

Sorry for how long it took us to get back to you on this, that's way too long and not like us.

Good news: planting milkweed in large pots and bringing them indoors for winter is absolutely doable, and it actually works well for your climate. A few things to keep in mind:

For SW Oklahoma summers, the species that tends to do best in containers is Asclepias tuberosa (Butterfly milkweed): it's drought-tolerant, handles heat well, and stays more compact than Common milkweed. Asclepias incarnata (Swamp milkweed) is another solid option if you can keep the soil a bit more moist.

For seed bombs planted in a pot rather than in the ground, I'd suggest placing each bomb just at the surface of the soil (no deeper than about 5mm), watering gently, and covering the pot with a clear plastic sheet or dome to create a greenhouse effect. This really helps with germination, especially when temperatures are already climbing. Keep them in a spot with good morning sun and some afternoon shade once the seedlings emerge.

One thing that might explain the past difficulties: milkweed seeds need cold stratification before they'll germinate reliably. Our seed bombs and stratified seeds come pre-stratified, so that part is handled, but timing matters. Planting when temps are already very high can push them past their ideal germination window. Since we're now well into summer, fall planting directly in the pot (left outdoors for winter, then brought in once established) may be your best bet this year.

If it helps, we now also offer cold-stratified seeds ready to sow here: https://lasclay.com/en/products/graines-semences-asclepiade-stratifiees-froid

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
